title: U.S. House · Georgia's 4th Congressional District
area: Parts of metro Atlanta east of the city, including DeKalb, Rockdale, and Newton counties.

context.text: Incumbent Hank Johnson (D), first elected in 2006, won the Democratic primary over Ansel Postell and Benedict Truman. James Duffie won the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Hank Johnson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over Ansel Postell and Benedict Truman.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 4th Congressional District (since 2007)

summary.text: Hank Johnson is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2006. A lawyer and former DeKalb County Commissioner, he is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C.; graduated from Clark College (now Clark Atlanta University) in 1976 and Texas Southern University's Thurgood Marshall School of Law in 1979.
Served as a DeKalb County Commissioner from 2000 to 2005, including as chair of the county's budget committee from 2002 to 2005; practiced law in Decatur, Georgia, for more than 25 years.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet Subcommittee; Oversight Subcommittee; The Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust Subcommittee) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: James Duffie
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: James Duffie is a U.S. Navy veteran and retired business executive, and the Republican nominee for Georgia's 4th Congressional District, campaigning for replacing the federal income tax with the FairTax and for stricter border enforcement.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Navy from 1961 to 1968; graduated from Avondale High School and attended the Georgia Institute of Technology; worked as a company president and CEO.

priorities.text: Says he will fight to eliminate the federal income tax and replace it with the FairTax, and to eliminate the IRS.
Says he will fight to keep borders secure and closed to unauthorized immigration.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to protect jobs by keeping the border secure, and that immigrants should assimilate.
Says Second Amendment rights should be protected.
